caption: Barnes v. Felix
proposition: Excessive-force reasonableness under the Fourth Amendment is judged on the totality of the circumstances, which has no time limit; the 'moment of threat' rule that ignores the events leading up to the use of force is rejected.

caption: New York v. Belton
proposition: On a lawful custodial arrest of a vehicle occupant, police may contemporaneously search the passenger compartment and any containers found within it, incident to that arrest.

caption: Terry v. Ohio
proposition: An investigative stop and protective frisk require reasonable, articulable suspicion grounded in specific facts and rational inferences, not probable cause.

caption: Riley v. California
proposition: The Robinson bright-line search-incident-to-arrest rule does NOT extend to the digital contents of a cell phone; police generally must obtain a warrant before searching a phone seized incident to arrest.

caption: Maryland v. Dyson
proposition: The automobile exception has no separate exigency requirement; if a car is readily mobile and probable cause exists to believe it contains contraband, police may search it without a warrant even with ample time to obtain one.
